newsitem.title: USA: Canadian natgas hits year-high on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian natgas hits year-high on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian natural gas prices hit their highest levels of the year Tuesday, propelled by an early blast of winter and dwindling storage supplies, traders said.
"They're staring in disbelief," said one Canadian trader. "Prices should stay up but probably not this high."

Gas for export to Sumas, Wash., sold around $2.15 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) for Wednesday delivery, while November prices surged to the mid-$2.40s, up from the low-$1.70s seen a week ago and up about $1.30 from October 1.
In early September, Sumas prices were in the low-$0.90s.

For several months, traders have argued that export prices in western Canada have been superficially low. Prices at Sumas have been averaging more than $1 lower than values at both Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, and Henry Hub, La.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Wednesday delivery jumped another five cents to the low-C$1.60s per gigajoule, up about 20 cents on the week and up 50 cents from October 1.
Despite recent below-freezing temperatures in the province, meteorologists are calling for milder weather by Thursday.

"It's still cold here, but it's supposed to gradually warm up throughout this week," said one Calgary-based gas trader, adding that large volumes of gas have been withdrawn from storage over the last several days.
As of October 18, the Canadian Gas Association said natgas stocks in western Canada were at 238.69 billion cubic feet, or 90.13 percent full, just shy of year-ago levels at 90.80 percent.
